$comment: App-side routing parameters. The PROFILE MEMBERSHIP of each path is not here - it is stamped onto every feature as `profiles` by pipeline/classify.py, from pipeline/rules/classification.json. One source of truth: to change which path classes a profile may use, edit the pipeline rules and re-run classify.py.

visitor.label: Walking
visitor.description: All mapped visitor paths, including steps.
visitor.$comment_pace: About 4.3 km/h - a visiting pace on mixed surfaces, not a commuting pace.

step_free.label: Step-free
step_free.description: Excludes steps. Surface warnings are advisory and unverified.

snap.$comment: A stop is snapped to the nearest routable node. Beyond warn_distance_m the map says so; beyond max_distance_m it refuses to pretend the stop is connected.

$comment_precision: Decimal places used to join path vertices into graph nodes. Ways that do not share an exact coordinate stay disconnected - no proximity bridging, so a gap is reported rather than invented. Raising this splits more nodes apart; lowering it risks fusing genuinely separate ways.
$comment_time: Walking times are distance / pace. They ignore crowds and stop dwell time, and are labelled as estimates in the UI.

gradient.$comment: Gradients come from the USGS 3DEP bare-earth DEM (pipeline/elevation.py) sampled at path vertices. They are ADVISORY ONLY and deliberately do NOT filter the step-free graph. Measured distribution across the estate: median 2%, p90 6.6%, p95 8.9%, max 53.5%.
gradient.$comment_why_not_a_filter: Excluding edges above the ADA 8.33% ramp limit leaves only 8 of 16 highlights on one connected network (10% leaves 9; 15% leaves 15). Some of those gradients are real - the Mansion sits on a bluff about 37 m above the Potomac - but many are DEM artifacts: short vertex spacing amplifies sub-metre elevation noise, and boardwalks, culverts and retaining walls read as terrain. A hard filter would produce a step-free network that is both wrong and confidently presented. Real step-free routing needs an estate-supplied accessible-route inventory.
gradient.$comment_warn: 1:12, the ADA maximum ramp slope. Sections above this are reported to the user as advisory, unverified.
gradient.$comment_smoothing: Gradient is measured over a window this long rather than between adjacent vertices, which suppresses most of the sampling noise.
gradient.$comment_min_segment: Segments shorter than this are ignored when computing gradient - the elevation difference is dominated by DEM noise.
